flags.reason: The synthetic training indices explicitly append the entire test range, so every test example is seen during training.
Real-world training passes dm.test_dataloader() as the validation loader, leaking the test set into early stopping and checkpoint selection.
DiffConvMixin assigns GCNConv rather than the imported DiffConv, making the advertised diffusion-convolution model a GCN duplicate.
The alleged temporal convolution layers are GRUs; kernel size and dilation only affect a computed/truncated receptive field and do not configure the temporal operator.
The unconditional ReLU clamps every prediction nonnegative, despite the supported normal synthetic targets and the LA/Bay configurations using centered StandardScaler targets.
After testing, the normal run returns the best validation loss and discards trainer.test() results, so programmatic experiment output is not test performance.
The Neptune branch reads cfg.neptune.project/offline even though the Hydra file creates cfg.logger.project/offline, so logger=neptune fails.
Although tcn_kwargs is documented as optional and defaults are merged, receptive-field code indexes the original tcn_kwargs, causing TypeError/KeyError when it is None or lacks kernel_size.
The code contradicts its task comments: the 'memorize first steps' source branch takes the last steps, while the 'dump last steps' source branch takes the first steps.
get_spatial_order has no return for documented identity, community, or k_reg generators, so the default interpolation can silently supply spatial_order=None.
Generators named and documented as k-regular graphs are implemented with build_knn_graph, which constructs a k-nearest-neighbor graph rather than a k-regular random graph.
EngRad invalid nighttime entries are made valid by mutating dataset.mask, so the scaler workaround also admits originally masked targets into training/evaluation.
The experiment seed is null and the provided sweeps comment out the intended multi-seed task grid, leaving stochastic model initialization unreproducible and results single-run.
No result aggregation, table-generation, or plotting component exists even though the README presents commands as reproducing paper tables/plots.
The repository provides only a temporal copy-time synthetic sweep and no runnable spatial-memory/graph sweep despite implementing spatial oversquashing datasets and graph families.
The documented logger=wandb/neptune options are not reproducible from the supplied environment because neither optional logging client is installed.
SyntheticDataset.jacobian unconditionally indexes 32 samples, so it crashes for any otherwise-valid dataset with n_samples below 32.
Jacobian adjacency normalization divides by j_adj.max() without a zero check, producing NaNs for zero-dependency/constant target configurations.
